newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong leadership contender woos Democrats.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong leadership contender woos Democrats.

text.p: A front-runner in the contest to lead Hong Kong after the British leave next year tried to bridge the gulf between China and the territory's Democratic Party on Friday, by calling on the group to join an interim legislature.
Shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa told reporters after meeting the Democrats they should come aboard the controversial provisional legislature for the good of Hong Kong.
"They should join the provisional legislature," Tung said.
"But even if they are not joining, they should give positive support to the provisional body," he said.

The party, a vocal critic of Chinese policies, has said it will not join the interim legislature which will be formed under China's supervision next month, and which will be installed next July 1 when Britain hands the colony back to Chinese control.
China, upset by the electoral reforms of Governor Chris Patten, has vowed to scrap the elected Legislative Council and replace it with the provisional body until new polls in 1998.
The Pro-democracy camp in Hong Kong has condemned China's plan as a way to snuff out democracy in the territory.
